resources.string: What are you here to do in %1$s?
Pick a time box — you\'ll get a gentle nudge when it\'s up.
Chosen apps stop interrupting you; their notifications wait quietly and arrive together at 8:00, 12:30 and 18:00. Conversations, calls and alarms always come through instantly.
Grant notification access to enable batching
One calm summary per batch of held notifications.
Nothing here. When batching is on, held notifications collect in this journal so nothing is ever lost.
From 22:00 to 07:00 the phone goes priority-only: starred contacts and repeat callers still reach you, everything else waits for morning.
Grant Do Not Disturb access to enable sunset
MindAnchor can estimate your sleep window from when the screen goes quiet at night — on this phone only, no wearable, nothing uploaded. Consistency matters more than hours.
Grant usage access to see your rhythm
Not enough nights recorded yet. Check back in a few days.
This is an estimate of how consistent your nightly phone-quiet window is — regular timing, not total hours, is what the research links to better mood and sleep.
Set MindAnchor as your home screen
Nothing hidden. Long-press any app to hide it from the drawer — it stays reachable by typing its exact name.
A calmer phone, built from published research. No accounts, no server — everything stays on this device. You choose what turns on; nothing is imposed.
What pulls at you? Pick what fits.
Apps I open without meaning to
My phone keeps me up at night
I want to know if any of this helps
Your plan — switch each on when ready:
• Notification batching (settings): chosen apps go quiet and arrive together three times a day. People always come through.
• Long-press any app and choose \"Add a pause\" — a breath and an intention before it opens.
• Sunset mode + sleep rhythm (settings): priority-only nights and a view of how regular your sleep is.
• The wellbeing pulse (settings): a 2-minute check-in every two weeks, scored honestly.
Explore at your own pace — every feature lives in settings and long-press menus, all off by default.
A 2-minute WHO-5 check-in every two weeks. It\'s how you — and MindAnchor — know honestly whether any of this is helping.
How have the last two weeks felt?
Five statements, answered 0 (at no time) to 5 (all of the time). This is a self-check, not a diagnosis.
0 = at no time · 5 = all of the time
Scores in this range are common when things are heavy. If it stays low, consider mentioning it to someone you trust or a professional — the support numbers are in settings.
Two weeks since your last pulse
MindAnchor never plays therapist. These reach real humans, any hour:
Elsewhere: findahelpline.com lists lines for most countries.

MindAnchor is an open-source, research-backed launcher. It has no accounts, no server and no analytics — your data never leaves this phone. It is a wellness tool, not a medical device. In crisis, reach a human: 988 (US) or Tele-MANAS 14416 (India).
